newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bertelsmann adds cash to AOL's Compuserve bid -WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Bertelsmann adds cash to AOL's Compuserve bid -WSJ.

text.p: Germany's Bertelsmann AG is adding cash to partner America Online Inc's offer to buy rival Compuserve Inc, the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday.
AOL's bid of about $1 billion in stock has so far been rejected by H&R Block Inc, which owns 80 percent of Compuserve.
The Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung reported Bertelsmann was interested in buying McGraw-Hill, which it said could be the reason for a sharp rise in the U.S. publishing group's share price.
Neither report named its sources. Bertelsmann officials were not immediately available for comment.
Bertelsmann operates AOL's service in Germany, and also packages AOL software in some of its music CDs.
AOL, which has about 8.5 million customers worldwide, is interested in Compuserve to pick up its three million customers, add to its corporate clients, and expand its network capacity.

Bertelsmann said in a statement that Woessner would take over as chairman of the company's supervisory board and the chairmanship of the Bertelsmann Foundation, which holds the majority of the company's stock.

Stephan Kruemmer, 40, will immediately take over Middelhoff's responsibilities for corporate development and multimedia, but will not have a seat on the management board. Kruemmer was previously on the board of book division Bertelsmann Buch AG.

A new three-member board will be created to guide the business divisions New Media and MediaSystems headed by Kruemmer and including Bernd Schiphorst and Michael Behrens and as so-called outside directors Middelhoff and Bertelsmann finance chief Siegfried Luther.

Schiphorst, 54, previously Middelhoff's deputy at the New Media division, will take over the operative leadership of the division, which includes Bertelsmann's partnership with America Online and the marketing of multimedia content and Interactive Studios.
